result.topic_en: A heavily corrected draft introduction arguing that partial differential equations are the foundation of physical theories, using terrestrial magnetism as an example, and that physics needs rigorous methods for integrating such equations which ordinary textbooks do not supply.

items.english: The real foundation of the theory of terrestrial magnetism is the law by which the direction and magnitude of the magnetic force change from place to place, a law entirely independent of how the causes of this magnetic force are arranged.
